note: Lean team: 3 roles (planner, implementer, reviewer), frontier-quality planner and reviewer, solid-coder implementer. NO model ids here — models are computed at GATE 1 from the live available list via recommend.py. Quality bars are role_tiers: planner/reviewer at 0.95 admit only near-best (frontier-class) models; implementer at 0.80 admits a good coder that wins on cost.

newest_only.note: Same newest-generation-per-family rule as the expensive roster; families without eligible routes simply drop out at init.

kb_namespaces.note: Lean roles reuse the expensive roster's curated corpora: each lean namespace searches multiple existing kb-sources dirs. No new content authored.

waves.note: Discovery: map existing codebase via graphify into out/planner/current-state.md

waves.gate: Verification gate: tests + acceptance criteria pass

roster_rules.brownfield: same 3 roles; wave 0 discovery precedes planning

planner.name: Planner (PM + Architect)
planner.when: Always first. Drafts charter, phased plan with task graph, module boundaries and ADRs (the architect's job in the expensive team).

implementer.name: Implementer (backend + frontend)
implementer.when: All code: server-side, client-side, CI config per plan.

reviewer.name: Reviewer (QA gate)
reviewer.when: Runs the verification gate against acceptance criteria; reviews the implementer's diff.

gstack_commands.note: OPTIONAL per-role methodology upgrade (same contract as the expensive roster): when the worker's host has gstack installed, the spawn prompt tells the worker to use these slash commands as its methodology INSTEAD of the generic built-in procedure. Without gstack, built-in procedure applies unchanged.
